A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete versions of the same survey, with readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison. The closing material in both consists of references; neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 surveys existing research. Its model and dataset compilations, VBench leaderboard and credited generation examples do not report original empirical outcomes produced by this survey.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. The added architecture, training, evaluation and ethics discussions describe cited work without introducing original experiments, user studies or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an original algorithm or model. The added GAN, temporal-attention, causal-VAE and training-pipeline descriptions explain existing methods rather than change a procedure developed by this work.

E1.justification: The dataset catalog in Table 2 is unchanged. New mentions of safety benchmarks and Cosmos applications expand literature coverage, without adding datasets or tasks actually used in experiments by this survey.

E2.justification: The reproduced VBench comparison retains the same methods. Newly discussed systems such as WAN and Cosmos are literature additions, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No existing experimental setting is revised and no new evaluation is conducted. Section 3.3 adds descriptions of WAN and Movie Gen evaluation criteria, while the new training diagrams provide additional documentation of cited systems.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis or empirical case study is added or removed. Existing credited qualitative examples remain; the new figures illustrate architectures and training workflows.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The benchmark reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The VBench leaderboard image is identical in v1 Figure 6 and v2 Figure 11. Tables 1–2 retain their entries and numerical values, and the existing qualitative result illustrations are retained. The additions describe methodology rather than new performance outcomes.

T1.justification: V2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the standard GAN minimax objective in Equation 1 and temporal scaled dot-product attention in Equation 13. Existing diffusion equations and guidance algorithms retain their mathematical content; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list and concluding core findings retain the same claims about the survey’s breadth, taxonomy, implementation coverage and connections to other domains. The expanded outlook does not redefine its central contribution.

C2.justification: V1 briefly flags bias and misuse; v2 adds a dedicated ethics section addressing consent, privacy, deepfakes, legal uncertainty, disclosure, safety and environmental costs. Section 7 substantially develops the earlier outlook with specific arguments about token efficiency, physical constraints, domain-specific applicability and hybrid models.

D1.justification: V2 supplies additional implementation information for surveyed systems, including causal-VAE compression, WAN filtering stages and training resolutions, and Movie Gen’s staged resolution and frame-rate settings. It also changes the listed GitHub destination from Eyeline-Research to Eyeline-Labs. These are documentation and access-information changes, not evidence of changed author-run experiments.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the reviewed literature around WAN, Cosmos, video safety, watermarking, physical plausibility and hybrid generation, especially through the new ethics section and referenced research agenda. Existing cited works are retained, and missing citation placeholders in Section 2.1.3 are filled.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the GAN subsection, adds explanatory transitions, inserts an ethics section and expands the outlook into titled bullets. The main taxonomy and organization of Sections 2–5 remain stable. Additional terminology, contact and publication-header edits are limited.

P2.justification: V2 adds five explanatory figures: temporal attention, ViViT, the CogVideoX VAE, WAN preprocessing, and Cosmos/Movie Gen training pipelines. Existing figures and both tables are retained with relocation and renumbering. The metrics diagram gains a motion qualifier, and the publication header changes the page layout.

improvement.justification: The added architecture illustrations and concrete training explanations make v2 more useful as a tutorial, while its ethics section develops deployment concerns only briefly addressed in v1. These gains outweigh localized new citation problems, such as naming Qwen2-VL while citing a Qwen-VL bibliography entry in Section 3.3. The central survey analysis and benchmark evidence remain largely unchanged, supporting a modest overall improvement.
